slides.headline: 2026 growth investment: fix retention before adding sales capacity
slides.reason_to_exist: Board deck opener naming the decision
slides.why_not_merge: Title slide: frames the decision, carries no argument

slides.purpose: Answer first: diagnosis, plan test, recommendation and asks
slides.headline: Churn, not sales, cut net new ARR by €5.6M; we recommend a retention-first plan at an estimated €2.0M a year instead of €3.6M for 30 AEs
slides.reason_to_exist: Gives the board the answer and the asks on one page
slides.why_not_merge: Executive summary: the answer and asks on one page for a board that may read only this slide
slides.assumptions_note: Figures depending on A001 (AE ramp), A002 (cohort size) or A003 (wave size) are marked as estimates / upper bounds on the slide

slides.purpose: Show where the slowdown came from in the ARR bridge
slides.headline: Higher churn explains 80.4% of the €5.6M fall in net new ARR; new-logo ARR still grew €0.2M
slides.reason_to_exist: The core diagnosis: the bridge shows the problem is churn and expansion, not acquisition

slides.purpose: Test the CRO's price-competitor diagnosis against the funnel
slides.headline: The sales engine did not break: pipeline grew 18.0%, deals won rose from 175 to 193 and only 31% of churned customers cite a competitor or price
slides.reason_to_exist: Rejects the management hypothesis that the CRO plan rests on
slides.why_not_merge: S3 shows where ARR was lost; S4 refutes the competing explanation the budget request is built on, and the board needs both to drop the price story

slides.headline: First-year customers churned 26% versus 12% in 2024 and supplied 60.3% of churned ARR; mature customers churned 9%
slides.reason_to_exist: Shows the leak is in the first year, which points to onboarding

slides.purpose: Link the leak to the onboarding cut and size its cost
slides.headline: Cutting onboarding saved €0.8M but more than doubled time to first value (21 to 48 days) and cost about €2.5M of ARR
slides.reason_to_exist: Root cause and its economics: the lever L1
slides.why_not_merge: S5 locates the leak (where); S6 explains it and prices it (why and how much), which is what the approve-€0.8M ask rests on

slides.headline: 30 AEs hired in Q1 deliver at most an estimated €4.5M in 2026, not €9M, because new AEs need 9 months to reach €300k (assumes a linear ramp)
slides.reason_to_exist: The board is asked to approve this plan; it must see that the promise does not hold
slides.assumptions_note: Figures depending on A001 (AE ramp), A002 (cohort size) or A003 (wave size) are marked as estimates / upper bounds on the slide

slides.purpose: Compare costed options and show levers versus the target
slides.headline: Retention first costs an estimated €2.0M versus €3.6M and identifies up to €5.3M of the €5.6M needed, leaving an estimated €0.3M gap (levers are upper bounds)
slides.reason_to_exist: Costed options and the lever bridge to the target, with the gap stated
slides.assumptions_note: Figures depending on A001 (AE ramp), A002 (cohort size) or A003 (wave size) are marked as estimates / upper bounds on the slide

slides.headline: Decisions today: reject 30 AEs, approve €0.8M for onboarding and a first wave of 10 AEs (our sizing), hold an estimated €1.6M until first-year churn is back at 12%
slides.reason_to_exist: Closes with what the board approves today and how it will be governed
slides.why_not_merge: Next steps: approvable asks, gates and KPIs; distinct from S8, which compares options
slides.assumptions_note: Figures depending on A001 (AE ramp), A002 (cohort size) or A003 (wave size) are marked as estimates / upper bounds on the slide
